 (SHRI S S CHOUHAN - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENTS  NO. 1 TO 4 AND SHRI MOHAN SAUSARKAR - ADVOCATE FOR  RESPONDENT NO.5)

This petition coming on for admission this day, Hon'ble  Ravi Malimath, Chief Justice passed the following:
 ORDER
The case of the petitioners is that the lands of the petitioners were acquired for the construction of four lane on the national highway by the respondents.

On an application filed by the petitioners under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, the Commissioner passed an award dated 29.10.2018 and remitted the matter to the respondent No.4 with the direction to conduct physical verification of the land.
Thereafter, a supplementary award was passed for an amount of Rs.20,38,848/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum for a period of 10 months.
The instant writ petition has been filed on the ground that the interest is liable to be paid by the respondents from the date of taking over possession till the payment has been made.
The respondents No.1 to 4 have filed their reply.
They have denied the claim of the petitioners.
They have stated that the appropriate interest has been awarded from the date of award for a period of 10 months.
They are not liable to pay any interest for the earlier period.
There are no submissions forthcoming from the counsel for the petitioners.
We have heard learned counsel for the respondents.

So far as, the National Highways Act, 1956 is concerned, Section 3(H)(5) thereof would indicate that compensation is to be paid to the petitioners and interest thereon from the date of taking over the possession under Section 3(D) till the date the actual deposit has been made.
The actual date of additional deposit is 18.06.2021.
Therefore, the supplementary award would necessarily substitute the original award.
Therefore, the rate of interest would have to be paid from the date of initial award dated 13.02.2013.
Therefore, the respondents are directed to pay the interest at the rate of 9% per annum from 13.02.2013 to 18.06.2021 and from 18.06.2021 till the balance amount is paid to the petitioners.
While calculating the same, the period of 10 months would have to be excluded.
